title: Olson and Söderqvist Discuss Valkey’s Evolution and Future Past Caching Use Cases at OSS EU
gist: Two years after forking from Redis, Valkey has 12 maintainers and a TSC across eight companies (AWS, Ericsson, Apple, Percona); maintainers describe ~4-5x throughput gains from async I/O, cluster improvements in v9, a Rust-core GLIDE client, and ambitions beyond caching via synchronous replication and SSD/S3 tiering.

insights.claim: More than two years after forking from Redis, Valkey has twelve maintainers and nine technical steering committee members across eight companies including Ericsson, AWS, Apple and Percona.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Multi-vendor backing, led by AWS, sustains a credible alternative to Redis after its license change.
insights.locator: More than two years after the fork

insights.claim: Valkey community conferences reach up to about one hundred participants, described as a young but growing project seeking more momentum.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Community remains modest in size relative to vendor backing.
insights.locator: More than two years after the fork

insights.claim: Valkey 8.x async I/O threading raised throughput from about 200,000-250,000 requests per second to around one million per process, with thread counts adjustable at runtime for bursts.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Large efficiency gains reduce cache infrastructure costs and strengthen Valkey vs Redis.
insights.quote: Async I/O threading increased throughput from approximately 200,000-250,000 requests per second to around one million per process.

insights.claim: Dual-channel replication sends the full dataset copy and the change stream in parallel, reducing memory pressure on primaries during replica sync.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Operational reliability improvement for large deployments.

insights.claim: Valkey 9 added numbered databases in cluster mode, atomic slot migration and hash-field expiration, removing barriers to migrating to cluster mode.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Eases scale-out adoption and competes on features Redis users requested.

insights.claim: Valkey GLIDE, which began as an AWS project, puts connection and topology handling into a shared Rust core with language bindings so a single core fix applies to all languages.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Rust shared-core pattern reduces client fragmentation; WebAssembly was judged too early.

insights.claim: Proposed directions beyond caching include synchronous replication for durability and tiering hot data in memory with colder data on SSD, possibly with backends like S3 or Postgres.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Valkey could expand into durable database territory, competing with broader data stores.

insights.claim: Cross-cluster active-active replication with eventual consistency is a longer-term idea, not an implementation commitment.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Avoid overestimating near-term Valkey enterprise geo features.
